t.1.28.1: Then, O best of the twice-born, when that tumult had arisen in such a manner, Garutmān, the king of birds, swiftly arrived before the gods.
t.1.28.3: And there was Bhauvana, of immeasurable spirit, whose splendor equalled lightning and fire, exceedingly mighty, the guardian of the Soma.
t.1.28.2: Seeing him, so exceedingly mighty, they trembled on every side, and they even struck all their weapons against one another.
t.1.28.4: Wounded by that lord of birds with his wings, beak and talons, he fought an unequalled battle for a moment and was then struck down in the fight.
t.1.28.5: And the sky-rover, raising a very great cloud of dust with the wind of his wings, made the worlds lightless and with it covered the gods.
t.1.28.6: Covered by that dust, the gods fell into confusion; and the guardians of the amṛta, shrouded by the dust, did not see him.
t.1.28.7: Thus Garuḍa threw the abode of the gods into turmoil, and with blows of his wings and beak he tore the gods apart.
t.1.28.8: Then the thousand-eyed god swiftly urged on Vāyu: "Scatter this rain of dust, O Māruta; this is your task."
t.1.28.9: Then the mighty Vāyu swiftly blew away that dust, and when the darkness had lifted, the gods assailed the bird.
t.1.28.10: And the mighty bird, whose cry was like the roar of a great cloud, screamed aloud as he was struck by the hosts of the gods, terrifying all creatures; then the king of birds, of great valor, slayer of enemy heroes, flew up into the sky.
t.1.28.11: Him, who had flown up and stood in the sky above the gods, all the armored deities showered with various weapons.
t.1.28.13: Though struck on all sides by the discharge of many kinds of weapons, the king of birds, waging a most tumultuous battle, did not tremble.
t.1.28.12: Together with Vāsava, the gods assailed him with spears, iron bludgeons, lances and maces, and also with blazing, razor-edged discs that had the form of the sun.
t.1.28.14: And the mighty Vainateya, roaring as it were in the sky, scattered the gods on every side with his two wings and with his breast.
t.1.28.15: Then those gods, scattered and tormented by Garuḍa, fled away; and, wounded by his talons and beak, they shed much blood.
t.1.28.16: Assailed by the lord of birds, the Sādhyas together with the Gandharvas fled to the east, and the Vasus together with the Rudras fled to the southern quarter.
t.1.28.17: The Ādityas made for the western quarter and the Nāsatyas for the northern quarter, looking back again and again as they fought the one of mighty strength.
t.1.28.20: The son of Vinatā, of great strength, tore them apart with the tips of his wings, talons and beak, like the enraged Pinākin at the time of the end of the age.
t.1.28.18: The sky-rover fought with the heroic Aśvakranda, with the winged Reṇuka, with the valiant Krathana, and with Tapana.
t.1.28.21: Those gods of great valour and great energy, wounded by him in many ways, shone like dense masses of clouds pouring down torrents of blood.
t.1.28.22: Having made them all lifeless, the best of birds passed beyond them for the sake of the amṛta and saw fire on every side.
t.1.28.19: He waged battle with Ulūka and Śvasana, with Nimeṣa and with Pakṣin, with Praruja and with Praliha.
t.1.28.23: It was a terrible fire of great blaze, fanned by the wind, enveloping the sky on every side with its flames, as though it were burning the sharp-rayed sun itself.
t.1.28.25: That blazing fire the scorcher of foes, the bird whose chariot is his wings, covered over with rivers; then, having quenched the fire and wishing to enter, he assumed another body, a small one.
t.1.28.24: Then the swift and great-souled Garuḍa made ninety times ninety mouths, drank up the rivers with those mouths, and came back again very quickly with great speed.
